chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (Allah) (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the fasting person who complains of his ear and pours medicine into it. He said: There is no problem with it.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no problem with it / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Does putting medicine in the ear break the fast in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that instilling medicine into the ear does not break the fast, establishing the principle that the ear is a distinct cavity separate from the throat. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between *ghurghara* (gargling) and direct instillation, emphasizing that the substance does not reach the stomach. It reflects the scholarly consensus that sensory organs like the ears are not considered pathways for nourishment in the context of fasting validity.
